findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id setting row is absent
findings.body: The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` and later `execute(...)[0]['value']` without checking whether the query returned any rows. On installs where these settings were never persisted, or where the old `embed_category` value does not match an existing category name, `execute(...)[0]` is nil and the migration aborts with `NoMethodError` before the host data is imported. The queries should use safe `first`/guard logic and fall back to the uncategorized category/default when absent.

findings.title: Migrated host strings are inserted raw and SQL-interpolated, breaking existing embeds
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting accepted values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (the old specs use exactly these), but this migration inserts each `h` verbatim into `embeddable_hosts.host`. The new lookup extracts only `uri.host` and compares it to the stored value, so migrated rows containing a scheme or path will never match and embedding will stop working after upgrade. The same line also interpolates the DB value directly into SQL, so a host containing an apostrophe will break the migration and untrusted DB content can inject SQL. Normalize host values with the same rules as the model and use bound parameters.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host instead of returning a validation error
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called before validation runs, so a new `EmbeddableHost` with a nil host (for example an admin POST missing `embeddable_host[host]`) raises `NoMethodError` and returns a 500 from the controller instead of an invalid-record response. The model should guard against nil/blank host before calling `sub!`.

findings.title: record_for_host compares lower(host) against a case-preserved, port-less URI host
findings.body: `record_for_host` extracts `uri.host` (which preserves the case supplied in the referer and excludes the port) and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` without lowercasing the parameter. A referer with an uppercase host will not match a stored lowercase host, and a stored host containing an allowed port (`example.com:3000`) will never match because `uri.host` is only `example.com`. This makes otherwise valid embeddable hosts fail the allow-list check. Normalize both sides and compare host without port, or store/compare consistently.

findings.title: All `*_ids` keys in rest_serializer payloads are now treated as embedded associations and can be corrupted
findings.body: The new `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` branch treats every key ending in `_ids` as an embedded association. If the payload has a `*_ids` key but no matching side-loaded plural collection, `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for every id, and the code still deletes the original key and replaces it with `[undefined, ...]`, silently losing the IDs. If the value is null or a non-array, `.map` throws. This affects any existing `__rest_serializer` response with `*_ids` fields, not just the new embedding payloads.

findings.title: Update/destroy assume the host exists and 500 on missing ids
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` both use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately dereference the result. If the id is stale or invalid, `update` calls `save_host(nil)` (which does `host.host = ...`) and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, producing a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find_by!`/`find` with a guard and render a not-found response.

findings.title: Embedded find test requests fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1 data
findings.body: The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but the pretender `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, with `color_ids: [1,2]`), and the assertions expect those color ids. The test therefore does not verify that the requested id is honored; if the pretender were corrected to return fruit 2 (banana, `color_ids: [3]`), this test would fail. Either the request id or the expected fixture should be corrected.

findings.title: New admin embeddable-hosts endpoint has no behavioral tests
findings.body: The spec only asserts that `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` subclasses `Admin::AdminController`. The new create/update/destroy behavior is untested: host and category persistence, defaulting a blank category to uncategorized, rejecting invalid hosts, handling missing nested params, and handling non-existent ids. This is why regressions like the nil-host crash and missing-record 500s are not caught.
